insulin-stimulated phosphorylations of calmodulin in vivo are enhanced by casein kinase-II, an insulin-sensitive serine/threonin kinase.
insulin stimulates the in vivo phosphorylation of calmodalin, and that calmodulin phosphorylated by casein-kinase II is a better substrate for the insulin-receptor kinase than unmodified calmodulin.
insulin stimulates calmodalin phosphorylation in intact hepatocytes and that calmodulin can be phosphorylated by both serine/threonie kinases and tyrosine kinases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of protein phosphorylation in intact hepatocytes and in vitro.
the role of calmodulin as a substrate for protein kinases.
the role of calmodulin and calmodulin kinase in insulin action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin stimulates the tyrosine and serine phosphorylation of calmodalin in vivo.
the phosphorylation of a protein by a receptor tyrosine kinase, in this case the insulin receptor, can be modified by phosphorylation of the protein by a different kinase.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
insulin stimulates calmdulin phosphorylation in hepatocytes and that calmodulin can be phosphorylated by the insulin receptor tyrosine kinase as well as by serine/threonin kinases.
insulin stimulates calmodalin phosphorylation in intact hepatocytes.
insulin stimulates calmo- din phosphorylation by the insulin receptor and casein kinase II.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calmodulin can be phosphorylated in intact cells by insulin and other hormones.
